holidays.name: World Snake Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the world's much-maligned legless locals. It's for anyone who thinks snakes deserve less screaming and more appreciation. Fans share photos, learn about local species, and remember that most snakes would rather avoid you completely.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial, informal observance started by reptile enthusiasts to promote snake conservation and counter fear and myths about snakes.
holidays.funFact: Snakes can't chew, so they swallow prey whole. Some species can open their jaws wide enough to eat animals bigger than their own head.

holidays.name: National Corn Fritters Day
holidays.description: A salute to golden, crispy-edged bundles of corn, batter, and deep-fried joy. Whether you like them sweet with syrup or powdered sugar, or savory with hot sauce, today is the day to heat up the skillet.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It fits neatly into mid-July, when fresh sweet corn is coming into season.
holidays.funFact: Corn fritters have a long history in American home cooking, especially in the South, where cooks have long turned cornmeal and kernels into quick fried treats.

holidays.name: Guinea Pig Appreciation Day
holidays.description: A day for the squeaky, wheeking, snack-obsessed little pets who greet every rustling bag of veggies like it's a parade. Owners are encouraged to give their cavies fresh greens, extra floor time, and plenty of admiration.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance of unclear origin, popular among small-pet lovers and guinea pig rescue communities.
holidays.funFact: Guinea pigs can't make their own vitamin C, so they need it from their food. Their happy squeaks are called wheeking.
